topics.title: Topic Particle は
topics.summary: は marks the topic of a sentence — written は but pronounced "wa".
topics.explanation: は marks the topic, what the sentence is about. It is written with the hiragana は but pronounced "wa". The basic pattern is "A は B です" (As for A, it is B).

exercises.promptTranslation: He is a teacher.
exercises.explanation: は marks 彼 as the topic: "As for him, he is a teacher."

exercises.prompt: この料理___おいしいです。
exercises.promptTranslation: This dish is delicious.
exercises.explanation: は marks この料理 as the topic.

exercises.promptTranslation: My name is Tanaka.
exercises.explanation: は marks 名前 as the topic.

exercises.promptTranslation: Japan has four seasons.
exercises.explanation: は sets 日本 as the topic: "In Japan, there are four seasons."

topics.title: Subject Particle が
topics.summary: が marks the grammatical subject, often introducing new or identifying information.
topics.explanation: が marks the subject that performs an action or is newly introduced. Use it (rather than は) to answer "who/what" or to point out specific information. Verbs of existence, perception, and ability also take が.

examples.text: 私は日本語がわかります。

exercises.promptTranslation: A student is in the library.
exercises.explanation: が marks 学生 as the subject that exists there.

exercises.promptTranslation: The cherry blossoms are pretty.
exercises.explanation: が marks 桜 as the subject being described.

exercises.promptTranslation: Who came?
exercises.explanation: Question words like だれ take が, not は.

exercises.promptTranslation: A sound can be heard.
exercises.explanation: Perception verbs like 聞こえる take が.

topics.title: Object Particle を
topics.summary: を marks the direct object of a verb, pronounced "o".
topics.explanation: を marks the direct object, the thing an action is done to. It is written を but pronounced "o". The pattern is "[object] を [verb]".

exercises.promptTranslation: He wrote a letter.
exercises.explanation: を marks 手紙 as the object of 書く.

exercises.promptTranslation: I listen to music.
exercises.explanation: を marks 音楽 as the object of 聞く.

exercises.promptTranslation: The child ate sweets.
exercises.explanation: を marks お菓子 as the object of 食べる.

exercises.prompt: 毎朝コーヒー___飲みます。
exercises.promptTranslation: I drink coffee every morning.
exercises.explanation: を marks コーヒー as the object of 飲む.

topics.title: The Copula です
topics.summary: です is the polite copula meaning “to be,” and its negative form is じゃありません.
topics.explanation: In polite Japanese, you attach です after a noun or adjective to say something is that thing. To make it negative, replace です with じゃありません. The sentence ends with the copula, so no extra verb is needed.

examples.text: それは高くありません。

exercises.promptTranslation: This is a pen ___ .
exercises.explanation: In polite speech, the copula is です.

exercises.promptTranslation: My name is Mari ___ .
exercises.explanation: Use です after a noun for polite introduction.

exercises.promptTranslation: It is rainy today ___ .
exercises.explanation: The adjective 雨です is expressed with the polite copula です.

exercises.promptTranslation: That is not a book ___ .
exercises.explanation: The negative polite copula is じゃありません.

topics.title: Polite Verbs -ます
topics.summary: Learn how to use the polite -ます form and its negative -ません in Japanese.
topics.explanation: The -ます ending makes a verb polite and is used in present/future statements. To make it negative, change -ます to -ません. Both forms are attached directly to the verb stem. Use them in everyday conversation to sound respectful.

exercises.promptTranslation: I drink coffee every morning (polite).
exercises.explanation: Use the polite present form -ます for a regular habit.

exercises.promptTranslation: I did not watch a movie yesterday (polite).
exercises.explanation: The negative polite form for past statements is -ませんでした, but for a simple negative past you need -ません after the past auxiliary, so the correct simple negative is -ません.

exercises.promptTranslation: I will ask the teacher a question (polite).
exercises.explanation: Use the polite present form -ます for a future/intended action.

exercises.promptTranslation: I am not doing homework now (polite).
exercises.explanation: The negative polite present -ません expresses a current negative action.

topics.title: Past Tense -ました / でした
topics.summary: Polite past tense in Japanese uses ました for verbs and でした for nouns/adjectives.
topics.explanation: To talk about something that happened, add ました to the verb stem. For negative past, use ませんでした. When describing nouns or adjectives in the past, replace です with でした. These forms are used in formal situations.

examples.text: 私は昨日本を読みました。
examples.romanization: Watashi wa kinō hon o yomimashita.

examples.text: 彼は日本へ行きませんでした。
examples.romanization: Kare wa Nihon e ikimasen deshita.
examples.translation: He did not go to Japan.

examples.text: その映画は面白かったです。

exercises.prompt: 昨日、友達とカフェでコーヒーを___。
exercises.promptTranslation: Yesterday, I ___ coffee at a cafe with a friend.
exercises.explanation: 飲みました is the correct polite past form of 飲む.

exercises.promptTranslation: She ___ good at Japanese.
exercises.explanation: でした is used to put the adjective 上手 in past polite form.

exercises.promptTranslation: I haven't read that book yet.
exercises.explanation: みませんでした is the negative past polite form of 読む.

exercises.prompt: 昨日の試合はとても楽しく___。
exercises.promptTranslation: Yesterday's game was very fun.
exercises.explanation: でした is the past polite form of です for describing the game.

topics.title: Existence あります / います
topics.summary: Use あります for non‑living things and います for living things.
topics.explanation: Both verbs mean “to exist.” あります is used with objects, places, and ideas that are not alive. います is used with people, animals, and other living beings. The particle に marks the location where something exists. The verb comes after the location phrase.

examples.translation: There is a desk in the room.
There is a dog in the park.

examples.text: 机の上に本があります。
examples.romanization: Tsukue no ue ni hon ga arimasu.
examples.translation: There is a book on the desk.

exercises.promptTranslation: There is a pen on the desk.
exercises.explanation: Pen is inanimate, so あります is used.

exercises.promptTranslation: There is a cat in the garden.
exercises.explanation: Cat is a living animal, so います is used.

exercises.promptTranslation: There is a teacher in the classroom.
exercises.explanation: Teacher is a person, thus います.

exercises.promptTranslation: There is paper inside the desk.
exercises.explanation: Paper is inanimate, so あります is correct.

topics.title: Particles に and で
topics.summary: Use に for destinations, time points, and existence; use で for where an action happens.
topics.explanation: に marks a destination (東京に行く), a point in time (9時に), or where something exists (机の上に). で marks the place where an action occurs (カフェで食べる) and the means used. Relative time words like 明日 take no particle.

examples.text: カフェで昼ごはんを食べます。
examples.translation: I eat lunch at a cafe.

exercises.promptTranslation: I am waiting at the station.
exercises.explanation: Waiting is an action at the station, so で.

exercises.promptTranslation: I go to Tokyo.
exercises.explanation: に marks 東京 as the destination of 行く.

exercises.promptTranslation: I read a book at the library.
exercises.explanation: Reading happens at the library, so で.

exercises.promptTranslation: I get up at 7 o’clock.
exercises.explanation: に marks the clock time 7時.

topics.title: Possessive の
topics.summary: の links two nouns, showing possession or relationship (A の B = B of A).
topics.explanation: の connects nouns: the first noun modifies the second. It shows possession (私の本 = my book), origin, or type (日本語の先生 = Japanese teacher). The pattern is A の B.

examples.romanization: kore wa watashi no hon desu.

examples.text: 東京の天気はいいです。
examples.romanization: Tōkyō no tenki wa ii desu.

exercises.promptTranslation: This is my pen.
exercises.explanation: の links 私 and ペン: "my pen."

exercises.prompt: 田中さん___車は新しいです。
exercises.promptTranslation: Mr. Tanaka's car is new.
exercises.explanation: の shows possession: "Mr. Tanaka’s car."

exercises.promptTranslation: He is a Japanese teacher.
exercises.explanation: の links 日本語 and 先生: "Japanese teacher."

exercises.promptTranslation: His name is Tanaka.
exercises.explanation: の shows "his name."

topics.title: The て-form
topics.summary: The て-form connects actions and makes polite requests with -てください.
topics.explanation: The て-form is made by changing the verb ending to て (or で). It can link two actions, showing sequence or simultaneity. Adding ください after the て-form makes a polite request. Use it after the verb stem, not after a noun.

examples.translation: I read a book and then slept.

examples.text: 音楽を聴いて、料理します。
examples.translation: I listen to music while cooking.

exercises.prompt: 朝ごはんを食べ___ください。
exercises.promptTranslation: Please ___ breakfast.
exercises.explanation: The verb 食べ needs the て-form 食べて before ください.

exercises.prompt: 宿題を終わら___、テレビを見ます。
exercises.promptTranslation: After finishing homework, I watch TV.
exercises.explanation: The verb 終わる becomes 終わらせて to link actions.

exercises.promptTranslation: I walk to the station.
exercises.explanation: 歩く changes to 歩いて to connect to the following clause or end the sentence.

exercises.prompt: 友達に手紙を書___、郵便局へ行きました。
exercises.promptTranslation: I wrote a letter to a friend and went to the post office.
exercises.explanation: 書く becomes 書いて to link the two actions.

topics.title: Want to -たい
topics.summary: Use the -たい form to say you want to do something.
topics.explanation: Take the verb stem and add たい. It works like an adjective, so it can be used with です or ですか. It only expresses the speaker's desire. For polite speech, attach です after たい.

examples.translation: I want to go to Japan.
Do you want to watch a movie?

exercises.promptTranslation: I want to go to the sea this weekend.
exercises.explanation: Add たい to the verb stem 行き to express desire.

exercises.promptTranslation: I want to read a new book.
exercises.explanation: Reading desire is expressed with 読みたい.

exercises.promptTranslation: I want to sing karaoke with friends.
exercises.explanation: Attach たい to the verb stem 歌い to show you want to sing.

exercises.promptTranslation: I want to study Japanese more.
exercises.explanation: Use 勉強したい to express the desire to study.

topics.title: い and な Adjectives
topics.summary: Japanese adjectives are divided into い‑adjectives and な‑adjectives, each with its own attachment and conjugation rules.
topics.explanation: い‑adjectives end with い and can directly modify nouns (e.g., 高い山). To make them negative, replace い with くない. な‑adjectives need the particle な before a noun (e.g., 静かな部屋) and use ではない for the negative form. Both types change similarly for past and polite forms.

examples.romanization: Kare wa genki na gakusei desu.

exercises.promptTranslation: This mountain is not tall.
exercises.explanation: The negative of an い‑adjective is formed by replacing い with くない.

exercises.promptTranslation: He is a ___ student.
exercises.explanation: な‑adjectives attach to nouns with な.

exercises.promptTranslation: The weather today is ___ .
exercises.explanation: い‑adjectives directly modify nouns without additional particles.

exercises.prompt: この部屋は静か___ないです。
exercises.promptTranslation: This room is not quiet.
exercises.explanation: The negative of a な‑adjective uses ではない.

topics.title: Plain Form (Casual Speech)
topics.summary: The plain form is the casual version of a verb — dictionary form, ない (not), た (did) and なかった (did not).
topics.explanation: Casual speech swaps the -ます forms for plain forms: 食べます → 食べる, 食べません → 食べない, 食べました → 食べた, 食べませんでした → 食べなかった. です becomes だ (often dropped), and い-adjectives simply drop です. Plain forms are also required before many patterns, such as と思う.

examples.translation: Are you going to see a movie tomorrow?

examples.text: 昨日は何も食べなかった。

exercises.promptTranslation: I'm not going to school today.
exercises.explanation: The plain negative of 行く is 行かない.

exercises.promptTranslation: I saw a movie with a friend yesterday.
exercises.explanation: A past action in casual speech uses the た form: 見た.

exercises.promptTranslation: Have you eaten already?
exercises.explanation: もう with a completed action takes the た form: 食べた.

exercises.promptTranslation: It didn't rain last week.
exercises.explanation: Past negative in plain form is なかった: 降らなかった.

topics.title: Potential Form (can)
topics.summary: The potential form says "can do": godan verbs change -u to -eru, and ichidan verbs swap る for られる.
topics.explanation: For godan verbs, change the final -u sound to -e and add る: 書く → 書ける, 話す → 話せる, 飲む → 飲める. For ichidan verbs, replace る with られる: 食べる → 食べられる, 見る → 見られる. The irregulars are する → できる and 来る → 来られる. The thing you can do is often marked with が instead of を.

examples.text: 納豆が食べられません。

exercises.promptTranslation: Can you go by yourself?
exercises.explanation: 行く is godan: -u → -eru gives 行ける → 行けます.

exercises.promptTranslation: I can write kanji.
exercises.explanation: 書く is godan: 書ける → 書けます.

exercises.promptTranslation: I can eat sashimi.
exercises.explanation: 食べる is ichidan: replace る with られる → 食べられます.

exercises.promptTranslation: I can play the piano.
exercises.explanation: 弾く is godan: 弾ける → 弾けます.

topics.title: Must -なければならない
topics.summary: -なければならない means "must / have to" — take the ない form, drop ない, and add なければならない.
topics.explanation: Replace the ない of the negative form with なければならない (or なければいけない): 行かない → 行かなければならない, 食べない → 食べなければならない, しない → しなければならない. In polite speech say なければなりません/いけません; in casual speech it shortens to なきゃ or なくちゃ.

examples.text: 明日は早く起きなければなりません。
examples.translation: I have to get up early tomorrow.

examples.text: 宿題をしなければいけない。
examples.translation: I have to do my homework.
I have to go home now.

exercises.promptTranslation: I have to take medicine.
exercises.explanation: 飲む → 飲まない → 飲まなければ.

exercises.prompt: 毎日日本語を___いけません。
exercises.promptTranslation: I must study Japanese every day.
exercises.explanation: する → しない → しなければ.

exercises.prompt: 八時までに会社に___なりません。
exercises.promptTranslation: I have to get to the office by eight.
exercises.explanation: 行く → 行かない → 行かなければ.

exercises.prompt: このレポートを今日中に___なりません。
exercises.promptTranslation: I have to write this report today.
exercises.explanation: 書く → 書かない → 書かなければ.

topics.title: If / When -たら
topics.summary: -たら means "if" or "when / once" — add ら to the plain past た form.
topics.explanation: Make the plain past form and add ら: 行った → 行ったら, 食べた → 食べたら, 安かった → 安かったら, 雨だった → 雨だったら. It marks a condition, or something that happens first before the main clause. The main clause can be a request, a plan or a past discovery.

examples.text: 雨が降ったら、家にいます。
examples.romanization: ame ga futtara, ie ni imasu.
examples.translation: If it rains, I'll stay home.

examples.text: 駅に着いたら、電話してください。
examples.romanization: eki ni tsuitara, denwa shite kudasai.
examples.translation: Please call me when you get to the station.
If it's cheap, I'll buy it.

exercises.prompt: 時間が___、遊びに来てください。
exercises.promptTranslation: If you have time, please come over.
exercises.explanation: ある → あった → あったら.

exercises.promptTranslation: If it's hot, please open the window.
exercises.explanation: い-adjectives use the past かった + ら: 暑かったら.

exercises.promptTranslation: Once I get home, I'll go straight to bed.
exercises.explanation: 帰る is godan: 帰った → 帰ったら.

exercises.prompt: 宿題が___、テレビを見てもいいです。
exercises.promptTranslation: Once your homework is done, you can watch TV.
exercises.explanation: 終わる → 終わった → 終わったら.

topics.title: Passive Form -れる/られる
topics.summary: The passive form -れる/-られる shows something is done to the subject, with the doer marked by に.
topics.explanation: For godan verbs change -u to -a and add れる: 読む → 読まれる, 言う → 言われる, 盗む → 盗まれる. For ichidan verbs replace る with られる: 食べる → 食べられる. する becomes される and 来る becomes 来られる. Japanese also uses a "suffering passive" when the speaker is negatively affected, as in 雨に降られた (I got caught in the rain).

examples.text: 先生に褒められました。
examples.translation: I was praised by the teacher.

examples.text: この本は多くの人に読まれています。
examples.romanization: kono hon wa ōku no hito ni yomarete imasu.
examples.translation: This book is read by many people.

exercises.promptTranslation: I was scolded by my mother.
exercises.explanation: 叱る is godan: 叱ら + れる → 叱られました.

exercises.promptTranslation: Someone stepped on my foot on the train.
exercises.explanation: 踏む is godan: 踏ま + れる → 踏まれました (suffering passive).

exercises.promptTranslation: My cake was eaten by my little brother.
exercises.explanation: 食べる is ichidan: 食べ + られる → 食べられました.

exercises.prompt: このお寺は八百年前に___。
exercises.promptTranslation: This temple was built 800 years ago.
exercises.explanation: 建てる is ichidan: 建て + られる → 建てられました.

topics.title: Causative Form -せる/させる
topics.summary: The causative form -せる/-させる means "make" or "let" someone do something.
topics.explanation: For godan verbs change -u to -a and add せる: 行く → 行かせる, 待つ → 待たせる, 飲む → 飲ませる. For ichidan verbs replace る with させる: 食べる → 食べさせる. する becomes させる and 来る becomes 来させる. The person made to act is marked with に (or を with verbs that take no object), and -させてください politely asks "let me…".

examples.text: 母は子供に野菜を食べさせました。
examples.romanization: haha wa kodomo ni yasai o tabesasemashita.
examples.translation: The mother made her child eat vegetables.

examples.text: 私にやらせてください。

exercises.promptTranslation: The teacher made the students read a book.
exercises.explanation: 読む is godan: 読ま + せる → 読ませました.

exercises.prompt: 父は私を一人で旅行に___。
exercises.promptTranslation: My father let me travel alone.
exercises.explanation: 行く is godan: 行か + せる → 行かせました.

exercises.promptTranslation: The manager made me work overtime.
exercises.explanation: The causative of する is させる → させました.

exercises.promptTranslation: Please let me rest a little.
exercises.explanation: 休む → 休ませる; -させてください asks for permission: 休ませてください.

topics.title: Honorific Speech (Keigo)
topics.summary: Keigo uses respectful verbs (尊敬語) to raise others and humble verbs (謙譲語) to lower yourself.
topics.explanation: Use 尊敬語 for the actions of customers, bosses or guests: いる/行く/来る → いらっしゃる, 食べる → 召し上がる, 言う → おっしゃる, 見る → ご覧になる. Use 謙譲語 for your own actions toward them: 行く/来る → 参る, 食べる/もらう → いただく, 言う → 申す, 見る → 拝見する. Most other verbs follow お〜になる (respectful) and お〜する (humble).

examples.text: 社長は会議室にいらっしゃいます。
examples.translation: The company president is in the meeting room.

examples.text: 何を召し上がりますか。
examples.translation: What would you like to eat?

exercises.promptTranslation: The teacher is going to Osaka tomorrow.
exercises.explanation: The teacher's action needs respectful 尊敬語: いらっしゃいます.

exercises.promptTranslation: I'll come to your office tomorrow.
exercises.explanation: Your own action toward others uses humble 謙譲語: 参ります.

exercises.prompt: お客様、こちらのケーキを___か。
exercises.promptTranslation: Would you like to try this cake?
exercises.explanation: The customer's eating uses 尊敬語: 召し上がります.

exercises.promptTranslation: Then I'll take a look at the documents.
exercises.explanation: Your own looking is humble: 拝見します.

topics.title: Change -ようになる / ようにする
topics.summary: ようになる describes a gradual change ("come to / become able to"), while ようにする describes a conscious effort ("make sure to").
topics.explanation: Attach ようになる to a dictionary or potential form to show a change over time: 話せるようになった (I became able to speak). Attach ようにする to a dictionary or ない form to show you try to make something a habit: 毎日運動するようにしている (I make a point of exercising daily), 遅れないようにする (I make sure not to be late).

examples.text: 日本語が話せるようになりました。
examples.romanization: nihongo ga hanaseru yō ni narimashita.
examples.translation: I became able to speak Japanese.

examples.text: 毎朝早く起きるようにしています。
examples.romanization: maiasa hayaku okiru yō ni shite imasu.
examples.translation: I make a point of getting up early every morning.

examples.text: 最近、子供が野菜を食べるようになった。
examples.romanization: saikin, kodomo ga yasai o taberu yō ni natta.
examples.translation: Recently my child started eating vegetables.

exercises.prompt: 健康のために、毎日野菜を食べるように___。
exercises.promptTranslation: For my health, I make sure to eat vegetables every day.
exercises.explanation: A conscious habit uses ようにする: ようにしています.

exercises.prompt: 一年勉強して、漢字が読めるように___。
exercises.promptTranslation: After studying for a year, I became able to read kanji.
exercises.explanation: A change in ability uses ようになる: ようになりました.

exercises.prompt: 忘れない___メモを書きます。
exercises.promptTranslation: I write notes so that I don't forget.
exercises.explanation: ように after the ない form means "so that … not".

exercises.prompt: 夜遅く食べない___しています。
exercises.promptTranslation: I try not to eat late at night.
exercises.explanation: ないようにする means "make sure not to".
